The owner chain: «First live test and self-drive» → «Windows-only live measurements» → the `another-os` residuals → this entry (census C-288 / C-729, 2026-11-08). A HYPOTHESIS carried since, not a recorded Linux fact.

- **On Linux openpty, the seam already delivers a key written right after a resize to a Rust child** — `spawn_delivers_a_key_written_right_after_a_resize_to_a_child_not_yet_reading` (`crates/viola-pty/src/lib.rs:886`) passes on CI's one `ubuntu-latest` leg (ci#44960846431 green): the key waits in the kernel tty buffer through the resize. What remains open is the CLI's own handling above the kernel.

- **viola's resize is polled, not signalled**: `RESIZE_EVERY` 250 ms (`pump.rs:13`). A human key typed into `viola run` right after a host resize reaches the child BEFORE the child's own resize, by up to 250 ms; the child sees «a key right after its resize» only for a key typed about one poll after the host's resize, or for a driver paste racing the poll.

- **The driver's send is gated on a redraw after a resize**: the size offered to the feed rebuilds the gate's screen blank (`gate.rs:53-61`, `screen.rs:336`), so a send whose gate wait spans the resize waits `QUIET_PERIOD` and, on a verified CLI, the redrawn input box. 1. **The grant** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/keys.rs`:
   - `Grant` gains `resize: bool`, set by the argv word `resize` (`--grant box,resize`); any other word still refuses
     the grant whole. A resize is no key: the closed `Key` set stays `Down · Enter · X · Del`.
   - `Keys` gains `may_resize()`, true only under that grant.
   - The X and DEL a round types after its resize go through the existing `type_key` with the frame read BEFORE the
     resize as its `on` (the box read up and empty there, `inputs#I2` item 3). No other readiness rule is added.
   - Inline cases (keeps tests S3, S4): `box,resize` grants both; `resize` alone grants no X; an unknown word refuses;
     `may_resize` is false under `box`.

2. **The model's resize** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs`:
   - `Model::resize(rows, cols)` sets the parser's screen size in place (vt100 0.16.2 `Screen::set_size`, which keeps
     the cells as a terminal does; `~/.cargo/registry/src/*/vt100-0.16.2/src/screen.rs:88`) and updates `cols`.
   - A poisoned model stays poisoned.
   - Inline cases: a fed box row reads `box: up` after a resize to 180×40 and back; a poisoned model reads `poisoned`
     after one.

3. **The round's pure parts** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`, beside `attr_counts` (no clock read, no I/O):
   - `KR_ROUNDS` = 12.
   - `kr_delay(n)` → 0, 20 or 100 ms, interleaved `0 · 20 · 100` from round 1, four each.
   - `kr_size(n)` → 180×40 on odd rounds, 210×45 (the rig's `screen::COLS` × `screen::ROWS`) on even ones, so the width
     changes every round.
   - `kr_round_word(typed, hint, first, again)` → `kept` when `first` equals the typed word, or `again` (the re-read
     after a further settle, `Some` only when `first` equals the hint word) does; `lost` when both equal the hint word;
     else `unread`.
   - `kr_reading(kept, lost, unread)` → `kept` at 12 kept; `lost` at one lost or more; else `unverified`.
   - Inline cases produce every word: `kept`, `kept` late (`again` the typed word), `lost`, `unread` (an
     `unread (no-box)` first), and the three readings; the schedule's 4·4·4 count and the size alternation.

4. **The arm** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs`:
   - `Arm::KR`, word `kr`; live labels `KR` · `KR8` and spares `KR-2` · `KR8-2` in `of_label` (`ledger::admit`'s
     `-2` rule).
   - Seeds as `HB`: `has_vhome` false, `verify_seed` false, `marker_seed` true, `trusted` true, `wrapped` None, pty
     the rig's 210×45.
   - `Session` gains `resize(size)`, which calls `PortablePty::resize` on its own pty (`viola_pty::Pty::resize`), then

     only, never screen text — security S3): `keys` (the `Keys::summary` word, `x 13, del 13` on a whole start),
     `box`, `modal`, `control`, `rounds` (rounds run), `kept` · `lost` · `unread` (each `{k}/12`), `kept-0ms` ·
     `kept-20ms` · `kept-100ms` (each `{k}/4`), `lost-at` (the delays a `lost` fell on, comma-joined, or `none`),
     `kr-reading` (`kept` · `lost` · `unverified`), `sizes` (`210x45-180x40`), `dirty-box` (`none` or the round), then
     the rig's own (`census`, `credentials`, `scratch`, `user-config`).
   - **`finish`'s whole-start rule:** a start is whole when the rig's own rule holds, `control` reads `told-apart`,
     `rounds` reads 12 and `kr-reading` is not `unverified`. So a `lost` reading still ends a whole start (exit 0): it
     is the measurement, judged by the round's reading entries, never the rig's red.
   - `parse`, `word`, `of_label`, the label and arm tables' cases, and the module doc gain the arm.

5. **The CLI** — `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs`: `kr` among `rehearse`'s words; `KR` · `KR8` (and
   spares) in `live`'s doc line, with one sentence: a plain `claude` whose own pty the rig resizes 12 times, one `x` and
   one DEL after each resize, no send.

6. **The rehearsals** — `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs`, in `rig_rehearsal_hb_…`'s shape, over the fake agent
   (`case.child(true, &[])`, `--screens`). Keeps tests S1–S4; security S1, S3.
   - `rig_rehearsal_kr_reads_each_key_kept_after_its_own_resize` (`--grant box,resize`):
     - exit 0;
     - `arm: kr`, `keys: x 13, del 13`, `control: told-apart`, `rounds: 12`, `kept: 12/12`, `lost: 0/12`,
       `kr-reading: kept`, `dirty-box: none`;
     - the fake agent's receipt holds a `size` line for 180×40 and one for 210×45 (the resize reached the child), and
       no `prompt` line (no send);
     - keys read from the rig's own `keys` word, never from the receipt (`test-plan ·
       decision/rig-no-key-read-from-keys-word`);
     - `assert_torn_down`.
   - `rig_rehearsal_kr_without_the_resize_grant_types_nothing` (`--grant box`): `refused: grant`, `keys: none`, no
     `size` receipt past the start's own, torn down.
   - The fake agent keeps every byte through a resize, so a red here is the arm's own.

title: B. The round — fired by implement under the cap, `leg` entries (`inputs#I2` items 2, 5, 7, 9)

data.head: ### B. The round — fired by implement under the cap, `leg` entries (`inputs#I2` items 2, 5, 7, 9)

body:
7. **Entries 6–19, in order:**
   - the host read, the two installs by path, `mise ls`, the census, the rig's build and its hash;
   - the kept products' sha set and the live home's stamp sha, read before the round;
   - `KR` (`--cap 1`), then `KR8` (`--cap 2`), each `--spare 1`, on one ledger
     `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize/evidence/kr-starts.ndjson`;
   - the two after-reads, then the two readings.

   **The two starts are ordered independent** (`inputs#I2` item 7): each version's reading is its own. A `lost` on `KR`
   is not a rig red, so `KR8` still runs; the reading entries 18–19 come last, and the first red among them stops the
   round there.

   A start that exits 1 (`refused shape`, `confounded`, `dirty-box`, `unverified`, the token window, a host stall) stops
   the round at its own entry. Its ledger line is read first; the spare (`KR-2` or `KR8-2`) is then a plan revision's
   entry on the overseer's word, never a re-fire of the base entry. A `lost` is never a spare's. A third base start is
   the operator's. On an account-limit refusal implement stops where it is (`inputs#I1` item 11).

8. **After the span:** the census keyed `operator` (entry 20). Then the ledger's two summaries read back, closed words
   and counts only (entry 21, report-only), copied by implement into
   `.andromeda/cache/chunks/2026-11-21-key-after-a-resize/evidence/live-round.md` from those typed fields alone. No kept
   frame is read into that file, a message, a log or the tree (`inputs#I2` item 6).

9. The whole integration layer, the smoke, `pre-push`, hygiene (which reads the evidence dir), the push and CI
   (entries 22–29).
- none
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/keys.rs` — `Grant.resize`, the `resize` word, `Keys::may_resize`, the grant cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/screen.rs` — `Model::resize`, its cases
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/rig/mod.rs` — `Arm::KR`, its labels and seeds, `Session::resize`, the round's pure parts, `arm_kr`, the summary keys, `finish`'s rule, the table cases, the module doc
- `crates/viola-e2e/src/bin/viola-live-rig.rs` — `kr` and `KR` · `KR8` in the doc lines
- `crates/viola-e2e/tests/rig_rehearsal.rs` — the two `KR` rehearsals
**The order.**

- Phase A: the formatter, the linter, the rig library cases, the `KR` rehearsals through the integration layer (which
  builds the root binaries they spawn), and the workspace unit layer.

- The round: entries 6–19, `round` and `live` entries ONLY (`inputs#I2` item 9). Its after-reads of state other actors
  move are keyed to the round.

- After the span: the census keyed `operator` and the report-only ledger read; then the whole integration layer and
  the operator pass.
**What is not run, and why.**
- No mutation run (`inputs#I1` item 10).
- No `--e2e` layer: no MCP, contract or path surface is touched; the rig is test-only.
- No release-check entry (CI's `release` job runs it).
- `cargo deny check` is CI's `supply-chain` job: no dependency is added.
- No product file changes, so no smoke beyond the operator pass's harness boot.

**Bounds.** Every test start runs under a test-owned home. Every waiting test takes a bound under the 20 s lint; the
rehearsals wait on the rig's exit under its `--deadline`. The live starts run under the rig's private scratch and
config; `--deadline 300` bounds each under its entry's `timeout`. The non-priming probes of each live leg are the round
entries ahead of it. The whole-round dry-run is shown on the P5 card.

**No remove-the-guard control** is planned: the chunk adds no product guard. The arm's `lost` and `unread` words are
made to fail by the pure cases of step 3 (entry 3), which produce each word from synthetic attribute words before any
graded use.

**The live atoms' must-pass readings** (validation check 4 (9)). The `KR` summary keys the live entries assert are
this chunk's own print site (step 4), so each word is read printed before any graded use, in block order:
- entry 3 runs the pure cases of step 3, which produce `kept`, `lost`, `unread` and the three readings;

- entry 4 runs the rehearsals of step 6, which print the arm's own keys (`arm: kr`, `keys: x 13, del 13`, `control:
  told-apart`, `rounds: 12`, `kr-reading: kept`) and the rig's teardown keys over the fake agent.

`kr-reading` on a real CLI is the reading itself, asserted only by the round's reading entries 18–19 (`inputs#I2`
item 4 names the predicate).

   - A pure predicate `settled_after(last_byte, mark, now, quiet) -> bool` (no clock read of its own): true only when
     `mark` is `None` or the last drained byte is LATER than `mark`, and `now − last_byte ≥ quiet`.
   - A new `Session::settle_since(mark: Option<Instant>, until, bound) -> bool`: the same 50 ms pump loop as `settle`,
     met when `settled_after(…, self.quiet)` holds and `until` admits the reading; ended as `settle` ends (the child
     exited while quiet, `bound`, a stop requested); its elapsed time pushed to `settles` (so `settle-ms` keeps every
     KR settle, the re-read's included).
   - `Session` gains `quiet: Duration`, set from the plan (step 10), `QUIET` (400 ms) by default.
   - **The mark** is the rig's own clock at the write: before each KR key, the session drains what is already queued
     (`pump(Duration::ZERO)`), the mark is taken, then `type_key` writes. Named residual: a byte the child wrote
     before the key but which reached the reader thread's channel between that drain and the write reads as after
     the key — a window of the drain-to-write gap alone.
